dana: Python draft snippet (async, different style):
```python
# examples/stream_replay.py
from redwood import AsyncStreamClient

client = AsyncStreamClient(api_key="${RW_KEY}")

async def handle(resume_token=None):
    async with client.open_stream(model="redwood-rlm", resume_token=resume_token, max_inflight=3) as stream:
        async for msg in stream:
            # msg.text, msg.token_index, msg.final
            process(msg)
            if should_pause():
                await stream.drain()  # let client catch up
    return stream.resume_token  # persist for next run
```
leo: TS sketch (async iterator + small control loop):
```ts
// examples/stream-consumer.ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })

export async function consume(resumeToken?: string) {
  const stream = client.startStream({ model: 'redwood-rlm', resumeToken, maxInflight: 5 })
  for await (const chunk of stream) {
    console.log(chunk.text)
    if (shouldThrottle()) await stream.drain()
  }
  return stream.resumeToken
}
```
ben: Go example using semaphore pattern (different from channel-only previously):
```go
// examples/replay.go
sem := make(chan struct{}, 6) // max_inflight
ctx := context.Background()
client := redwood.New()
resume, _ := loadResume()
stream, err := client.OpenStream(ctx, redwood.StreamOptions{Model: "redwood-rlm", ResumeToken: resume, MaxInflight: 6})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for {
  sem <- struct{}{} // acquire slot
  chunk, err := stream.Recv()
  if err == io.EOF { break }
  go func(c redwood.Chunk) {
    defer func(){ <-sem }() // release
    fmt.Print(c.Text)
  }(chunk)
}
// persist stream.ResumeToken()
```
